scope: Proposition 3.2 (Comparison with pins and wires) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The finite (s, W) law is positively associated in (3.3), as is every conditional law obtained by fixing vertex spins and compatible edge states with both endpoints fixed. Increasing additional vertex and compatible edge prescriptions, or changing retained connections according to the ordered boundary rule, increases the residual law. The analogous statement holds with the two colors reversed. These comparisons permit monotone circuit couplings: search from the changed data toward the region of interest, and stop at an open plus circuit in the lower configuration, or an open minus circuit in the upper configuration. Beyond such a common cut, the two configurations, including complementary cluster colors, can be sampled identically.
